To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pin modulus is the most important parameter in EFF frame design and that the pin modulus and the side‐bar separation are the most important frame parameters to control frame rigidity and pin stresses.

the frame rigidity in EFF configurations can be adapted to a realistic range from about 13 to 17, 000 N/mm, by varying the frame characteristics, thereby reducing the stresses in the pins by a factor of about 140, and that this can be done without significantly affecting the peak stresses at the pin– bone interface.

the frame rigidity, the pin stresses, and the peak bone stresses in external fracture fixators can be controlled by adjusting the frame characteristics, and that the frame characteristics can be adapted to reduce the stresses in the frame and at the pin/bone interfaces without compromising frame rigidity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
external fracture fixation (E.F.F.) in bone.
the development of simple approximate formulas to predict frame rigidity and pin stresses in EFF configurations in axial loading.
the mechanical aspects of external fixation (EF).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the frame rigidity can be varied by orders of magnitude, thereby reducing the stresses in the frame and at the pin‐bone interface by a similar factor.

the frame rigidity, and hence the maximal stresses in pins and at pin–bone interfaces, can be controlled by a number of parameters in a realistic EFF configuration, and that the frame rigidy can be reduced by 99% while only moderately increasing stresses in the pins.
EFF frames are very flexible and that pin stresses can be kept low, provided that a few basic rules are followed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EFF configurations are very flexible and adaptable, and can be designed to meet specific requirements.
, in EFF, the frame can be made more flexible by reducing the pin modulus, increasing the side‐bar separation, or increasing the number of side bars.

the frame rigidity can be adapted to a large extent by the side‐bar separation, the pin diameter, the pin length, and the pin modulus; that pin stresses are mainly determined by the pin diameter, pin length, and frame rigidity, but are also influenced by the pin modulus, pin diameter, and side‐bar separation; and that bone stresses are mainly determined, in addition to pin stresses, by the pin modulus and pin diameter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pin–bone stress values can be reduced by a factor of about 100 by increasing the pin modulus and decreasing the frame rigidity.

the frame characteristics, such as the pin modulus, the pin length, the side‐bar separation, and the side‐bar thickness can be adapted to reduce the rigidity and stresses in the pins while maintaining a flexible frame.
the pin–bone contact area is the most important parameter for determining the pin stress, which is in agreement with the results of previous studies.
